channelTitle: By square 40 the treasurers went pale - the math of the rice chessboard - Part 2
hook: In Part 1, the emperor laughed and agreed to pay in rice - doubled each square. Then the treasurers started the real math.
storyParts: By the twentieth square the court stopped laughing. By the thirtieth, the treasurers were emptying granaries. By the fortieth they went pale: the squares demanded more rice than the empire harvested in a decade.
The sixty-fourth square alone - eighteen quintillion grains - needed more rice than the world had ever grown. The humble request was the most expensive bargain in history.
Some versions of the tale end kindly: the emperor, impressed, made the inventor his chief advisor and paid him honestly what the treasury could bear.
The darker versions end with an executioner - emperors don't enjoy being outsmarted in front of the whole court. Either way, nobody ever mocked a modest request again.
Mathematicians still teach the story today. It's the oldest cautionary tale about exponential growth - and it fit on a board you could carry in one hand.
moral: Grandma June's takeaway: never laugh at a small number that's doubling - it's how most fortunes and most debts are really made.
cta: Would you have taken the rice deal? Tell Grandma June what you'd have asked for instead
